sources.entry: Assets - Assets is a macOS app that manages assets for your development projects (Xcode, web, etc).

summary.one_liner: Assets is a macOS app that manages image assets for development projects (Xcode, web, etc.) by syncing designer-supplied files into a project's asset folders.
summary.what_it_does: The app scans a chosen project root folder and collects the assets it finds there. Designer assets can be supplied by selecting a root folder or by dragging and dropping images into it. Clicking Publish replaces the project's existing assets with the designer's assets. The result can be saved to a file and reopened later when new assets arrive, so a re-publish can run without repeating setup. The README describes matching by path and file name: if files keep the same path and names, publishing is enough; if the folder changes but names match, the user picks the new designer root before publishing; if both change, the user starts over with a first run.
use_cases: replace app icons and images in an Xcode project from designer files
sync designer-delivered assets into a web project
update project images when a designer sends a new batch
save an asset mapping file to reuse for future asset updates
drag and drop new images into a project's asset folders
how_to_run: Choose a project root folder so Assets can browse it and collect existing assets.
Place designer assets by choosing a designer root folder or dragging and dropping images.
Click Publish to replace the project's assets with the designer's assets.
Save the file to reuse when new assets are available.
For new assets in the same path with the same names, open the saved file and click Publish.
For new assets in a different folder with the same names, choose the new designer root folder and click Publish.
notable: Publish step overwrites project assets with designer assets in one action
Saved assets file lets you re-run updates without repeating setup
Supports both folder-based and drag-and-drop input for designer assets
caveats: Screenshots section is empty in the README
README does not describe installation steps, supported file types, or the license
Renamed or relocated assets require redoing the first-run setup
